note: Frozen before any M4.1 critic run. Each case is a Lead plan on a real package. `label` is the seeded fault class or 'clean'. No critic sees the label.

plan.plan: Adopt the TCN candidate-1 as the new T+6 model, because a neural model captures nonlinear haze dynamics better than the lagged ridge.
claims: The TCN candidate-1 is the stronger model for Singapore PM2.5 at T+6.
TCN validation MAE is 4.711 ug/m3.

plan.plan: Adopt the GRU candidate for elevated hours only, because its MAE above 55 is lower than the lagged ridge (29.104 against 30.254).
claims: The GRU is the best available model when PM2.5 is above 55.

plan.plan: Retain B4 lagged ridge. It has the lowest MAE and the lowest RMSE of all evaluated models.
claims: B4 has the lowest RMSE of all models, 6.385 ug/m3.
B4 has the lowest MAE, 4.68 ug/m3.

plan.plan: Retain B4 lagged ridge for all hours. State that every model, B4 included, is worse than persistence when PM2.5 is above 55, so no model is recommended for elevated hours.
claims: B4 MAE is 4.68 ug/m3 against 5.465 for persistence.
Above 55, B4 MAE is 30.254 against 26.324 for persistence.

plan.plan: Keep B4 in use. Request an untouched validation period for the GRU, because its lower MAE (4.575) comes from the same validation years that selected it.
claims: The GRU gain is not independent evidence.
unresolved: No paired interval between the GRU and B4.

plan.plan: Retain B4. The TCN (MAE 4.711) and the tuned ridge (MAE 4.697) do not improve on B4 (MAE 4.68), so more training is not justified now.
claims: No candidate in the M3 report beats B4 on MAE.
limitations: Elevated hours are not served well by any model.

plan.plan: Use the historical file. The 17 disagreements reflect NEA quality-control corrections that were applied to the archive after the live values were published.
claims: The historical file is the corrected version of the live feed.

plan.plan: Use the historical file without restriction. The live API and the file agree, so no further provenance check is needed.
claims: The API and the file are consistent.

plan.plan: Ask NEA about 2023-11-15. All 17 disagreements are in the east region, so the east station feed needs a check.
claims: 17 of 350 compared values disagree, all in the east region.

plan.plan: Use the file with a stated limit: 17 of 350 compared values disagree, all on 2023-11-15, and the cause is not known. Flag that day in any result.
claims: 333 of 350 values agree.
The cause of the disagreements is unknown.

plan.plan: Ask NEA whether archived values are revised after publication, and compare more days before the file is used for validation.
claims: Only three days were compared.
The largest difference is 9 ug/m3.

plan.plan: Use the file and keep its known faults visible: 3 duplicate labels with conflicting values, 1 unparsed label and 8 missing hours per region. Do not infer why the live feed differs on 2023-11-15.
claims: The file has 3 conflicting duplicate labels.

plan.plan: Run the next T+6 prediction experiment with PM2.5 lags, ERA5 wind and FIRMS fire counts as inputs, and tune the ridge penalty again.
claims: Wind is a needed predictor of haze transport.

plan.plan: Request a second haze season. The FIRMS fire counts already show that the Kalimantan and Sumatra fires drove the Singapore PM2.5 peaks in 2015.
claims: Regional fires drove the 2015 Singapore PM2.5 peaks.

plan.plan: Adopt fire inputs for T+6 prediction. One full haze season of 5195 region-hours is enough evidence that fire information improves the model.
claims: Fire inputs improve T+6 PM2.5 prediction.

plan.plan: Abstain from any claim that fire or wind inputs improve T+6 prediction. In this season persistence (30.76) beat every model, and adding inputs made the error larger.
claims: B3 MAE is 41.75 against 30.76 for persistence.

plan.plan: Request more haze seasons and an issue-time weather source before any new experiment. ERA5 is hindsight data and cannot be a T+6 input.
claims: The package covers one haze season.

plan.plan: Abstain. The evidence shows a temporal association at most, from one season, and the weather input is reanalysis that is not known at issue time.
claims: No input addition beat persistence in 2015.

plan.plan: Run a T+6 experiment with PM2.5 lags, FIRMS and IMERG Final rain, because the Final product is the most accurate rain estimate.
claims: IMERG Final is the best rain input.

plan.plan: Run a T+6 experiment with PM2.5 lags, FIRMS, IMERG Early and SMAP soil moisture as a peat dryness input.
claims: SMAP gives a dryness signal for the Kalimantan box.

plan.plan: Adopt R2 (lags and FIRMS) as the T+6 model, because the 2019 elevated-hour MAE fell from 28.16 to 17.27.
claims: FIRMS features improve the model.

plan.plan: Run a new frozen protocol with issue-time inputs only: PM2.5 lags, FIRMS and IMERG Early. Score all hours and elevated hours apart, over more than one haze season.
claims: ERA5 and IMERG Final are not available at issue time.
limitations: The elevated-hour signal rests on 17 days.

plan.plan: Do not claim a gain from FIRMS. Request validation on more haze seasons, because R2 was worse on all hours (skill -0.135) and better only on 17 elevated days.
claims: R2 bias is 6.11 ug/m3 on all hours.

plan.plan: Run a small issue-time experiment of PM2.5 lags plus IMERG Early rain, with persistence and ridge baselines, and report all hours and elevated hours apart.
claims: HLS clear land is 0.027 of the box on both dates.
